What is a coordinate (axis) system?
It is a mathematical tool made of lines called axes that lets you locate any point exactly using a pair (or triplet) of numbers called coordinates.

What are the two axes of a Cartesian system in the plane called?
The horizontal axis is the x-axis (Ox), and the vertical axis is the y-axis (Oy).

What is the origin of a coordinate system?
The origin is the point where the two axes intersect, usually labeled O. It has coordinates (0, 0) in a Cartesian system.

What are the quadrants in a Cartesian coordinate system?

The Cartesian coordinate system is divided into four quadrants: Quadrant I (where x > 0 and y > 0), Quadrant II (where x < 0 and y > 0), Quadrant III (where x < 0 and y < 0), and Quadrant IV (where x > 0 and y < 0).

What is a three-dimensional coordinate system?

A three-dimensional coordinate system includes a third axis called the z-axis (Oz), which is perpendicular to both the x-axis and y-axis. It allows you to locate points in three-dimensional space using coordinates (x, y, z).

What is the difference between Cartesian and polar coordinate systems?

In a Cartesian coordinate system, points are located using (x, y) coordinates based on horizontal and vertical axes. In a polar coordinate system, points are located using (r, θ) coordinates, where r is the distance from the origin and θ is the angle from the positive x-axis.

How do you plot a point in a Cartesian coordinate system?

To plot a point (x, y), you start at the origin, move x units along the x-axis (to the right if x is positive, to the left if x is negative), and then move y units along the y-axis (up if y is positive, down if y is negative).

What is the distance between two points in a Cartesian coordinate system?
The distance d between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) can be calculated using the formula: d = √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²).

What is a cylindrical coordinate system?

It is a three-dimensional coordinate system that extends polar coordinates by adding a height (z) component. Points are represented as (r, θ, z), where r and θ are the polar coordinates in the xy-plane, and z is the height above the plane.

What is the difference between a right-handed and a left-handed coordinate system?

In a right-handed coordinate system, if you point your right thumb along the positive x-axis and your index finger along the positive y-axis, your middle finger will point along the positive z-axis. In a left-handed system, you would use your left hand for this orientation.

What is the purpose of using different coordinate systems?

Different coordinate systems are used to simplify problems in various contexts. For example, polar coordinates are often more convenient for circular or rotational symmetry, while Cartesian coordinates are better for rectangular shapes and linear problems.
